newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-REGGIANA TAKE ON UNTRIED COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REGGIANA TAKE ON UNTRIED COACH.

text.p: Francesco Oddo, a Sicilian coach who has no serie A experience, took over bottom-of-the-table Reggiana on Tuesday after Romanian Mircea Lucescu was sacked.
Reggiana said Oddo, formerly with serie B sides Avellino, Modena and Pescara, had signed a two-year contract and would lead his first training session on Wednesday.

"Safety? It's a very difficult task, for some it looks desperate. But if I am here its because I hope to do it -- I am confident," the new coach said, identifying the battle against relegation as his main task.
"They have asked me to bring enthusiasm and motivation, not safety at all costs," Oddo added.
Reggiana were promoted at the end of last season when current Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti was at the helm. They decided to replace Lucescu on Monday.
"I am sorry to be always turning up like this," said Oddo. "Lucescu is a very good coach."

The provincial northern club stands alone as the only serie A team yet to win a match this season. They have four points from 10 games and are firmly embedded in the floor of the division with only nine goals to their credit -- the lowest tally in Italy's top division.
"I am not frightened (of coaching in serie A for the first time)," said Oddo. "I am used to working with teams fighting for safety. So far I have always done a good job."

Lucescu, who arrived in Italy from Dinamo Bucharest in 1990 when he took over as coach of Pisa, has been dismissed three times in seven years in Italian soccer. Pisa fired him in 1991 and he moved to Brescia, where he stayed in charge until 1995.
